name: AuditCore hackathon rubric v3
note: v3 assumes most teams use AI coding tools. Clean code, tests and tidy structure are what those tools produce by default, so polish criteria are CAPPED for the AI reviewer (baseline_cap) and the weight moves to system design, completeness and innovation. Documentation is not scored. Criteria with ai_assisted=true are pre-scored from the repository by AuditCore; the rest need a human judge. Scores are 0-10. Organizers should edit weights per event.

criteria.title: System design & architecture
criteria.description: Not 'is the code clean' (AI tools write clean code) but 'were deliberate design decisions made?'. Look for: a data model that fits the problem, sensible component boundaries, a justified choice of storage/queue/cache/API style, how state and failures are handled, how the parts scale or degrade, integration of several real components, and trade-offs that show the team understood the problem rather than accepting a default scaffold. List each decision you can evidence in design_decisions. Scaffold defaults (a generated CRUD app, the default framework layout, a single API call wrapped in a route) are the BASELINE and earn at most 5. Scores above 5 need verified evidence of specific decisions; the AI reviewer's maximum is 8, and 9-10 are for human judges after they have questioned the team.
criteria.cap_formula: 5 + number of verified design_decisions, at most 8

anchors.2: Boilerplate or a thin wrapper around one API; no visible design choices.
anchors.5: A generic, working scaffold: sensible layout, but every choice looks like a framework default.
anchors.8: Several specific, evidenced decisions (data model, boundaries, failure handling, integration) that fit this problem.

criteria.title: Innovation & creativity
criteria.description: Novelty compared with existing solutions: a new idea, an unusual combination, or a clearly better way to do a known thing. Judged by a human. AuditCore supplies the 'Where this stands' landscape note (closest existing projects and how this one differs) as evidence, never as a score.

criteria.title: Completeness & working end to end
criteria.description: Evidence that one complete user path actually works: routes/handlers wired to real logic, persistence, error states where relevant, run/deploy configuration. Penalize hard-coded or pre-loaded data that only works for a demo, placeholder content, and features that are claimed but not in the code.

anchors.2: Parts do not connect, data is hard-coded or fake.
anchors.5: The main flow appears wired end to end but with gaps or demo-only data.
anchors.8: Full flow with real persistence/integration, error states, and run configuration.

criteria.title: Impact & usefulness
criteria.description: A clearly defined user, a real problem, and plausible adoption. Judged by a human.

criteria.title: Demo & presentation
criteria.description: Live demo works, clear story, realistic data, honest answers to the design questions. Judged live by a human.

criteria.title: Code quality
criteria.description: Structure, modularity and readability. AI tools make this look good by default, so the AI reviewer cannot score above 7; judges may.

anchors.7: Clean modules and consistent style (typical of AI-assisted code).

criteria.title: Robustness & error handling
criteria.description: Input validation, failure handling, tests that test something real. Generated boilerplate tests and try/except wrappers are the baseline; the AI reviewer cannot score above 7.

anchors.5: Basic error handling on main paths; few or no tests.
anchors.7: Validated inputs, handled failures, meaningful tests.

criteria.title: Security & secrets
criteria.description: Secrets handled via environment variables, no committed credentials, no obvious injection/XSS. Static findings provided are facts. Committed secrets are a real problem and are scored here and flagged; missing documentation about them is not.

anchors.2: Committed secrets or obvious injection holes.
anchors.5: No leaked secrets; some unsafe patterns.
anchors.8: Config via environment; no unsafe patterns found.

red_flags_for_judges: Slides or mockups with no working code behind them
Hard-coded or pre-loaded data so the demo only works for one input
A thin wrapper around a single third-party API presented as the product
Elaborate UI with little backend or logic behind it
Pitch claims that the code does not support
Work that predates the event presented as built during it
Generic clone ('another todo app', 'another chatbot') with no differentiation
The team cannot explain why they chose their data model, storage or architecture
